# For instructors and editors {.unnumbered}

This appendix is for people who maintain this edition of the book, not for
students. It records how the repository is organised, how the book is built,
how to pull in updates from the original author, and what the license allows.

## Where things are

The repository is a fork of Dr. Chuck Severance's
[csev/py4e](https://github.com/csev/py4e) repository, which holds the
py4e.com website and the master source of the book. Its structure is left
untouched so that upstream updates merge cleanly. Everything specific to this
edition lives in one folder, `yr-materials/`:

| Path | What it is |
|------|------------|
| `_quarto.yml`, `index.qmd` | The Quarto book project. Chapters are listed here. |
| `py4e-quarto/*.qmd` | **Generated** chapters converted from upstream `book3/*.mkd`. Do not hand-edit; see below. |
| `py4e-quarto/images/` | Figures copied from upstream by the converter. |
| `my-content/chapters/` | Chapters written for this course. Safe to edit freely. |
| `my-content/notebooks/`, `my-content/exercises/` | Notebooks and exercise sets for students. |
| `for-editors.qmd` | This appendix. |
| `tools/` | Scripts for converting, building, syncing, and scaffolding (listed below). |
| `../.claude/skills/` | Claude Code skills that wrap the tools. |

Reusable material in the upstream part of the repository:

| Upstream path | Contents |
|---------------|----------|
| `book3/*.mkd` | Book text, one Pandoc-markdown file per chapter (the master source). |
| `code3/` | Every example program and data file the book refers to. |
| `images/`, `book3/figs2/` | Figures as svg, png, and eps. |
| `html3/` | Pre-built HTML of each chapter, for reading only. |
| `lectures3/` | Lecture slides as pptx and pdf. |
| `assn/` | Assignment descriptions used on py4e.com. |
| `lessons.json` | Mapping of chapters to videos and assignments on py4e.com. |

## Git remotes

| Remote | URL | Use |
|--------|-----|-----|
| `origin` | https://github.com/y-rosenthal/py4e | Our fork. Push work here. |
| `upstream` | https://github.com/csev/py4e | Dr. Chuck's repository. Pull updates from here. |

Work happens directly on `master`. Because our changes are confined to
`yr-materials/`, `.gitignore`, `CLAUDE.md`, and `.claude/`, merging upstream
never conflicts with our content.

The clone is about 2 GB because upstream tracks slides and media. The
repository lives inside Dropbox; Dropbox and Git can corrupt each other while
both are writing to `.git/`. Either keep the repository out of Dropbox or tell
Dropbox to skip the Git internals:

```bash
attr -s com.dropbox.ignored -V 1 .git
```

## How the generated chapters are made

`tools/mkd2qmd.py` reads each upstream chapter in `book3/` and writes a clean
`.qmd` into `py4e-quarto/`. It:

- strips the LaTeX `\index{}` entries;
- turns `~~~~ {.python .trinket}` fences into standard ```` ```python ```` fences;
- replaces `\VerbatimInput{../code3/foo.py}` with the file's contents plus a
  comment giving the file's URL on py4e.com;
- replaces `\begin{trinketfiles}` blocks with a callout that links the data
  files an example needs;
- converts figures to `![Caption](images/foo.svg){height=...}` and copies the
  image;
- turns figure `\label{}` and `\ref{}` into Quarto cross references;
- converts setext headings to ATX (`#`) headings;
- adds an HTML comment with source and license attribution at the top.

Re-run it whenever upstream changes:

```bash
python3 yr-materials/tools/mkd2qmd.py          # all chapters
python3 yr-materials/tools/mkd2qmd.py 04 05    # just chapters 04 and 05
```

If a generated chapter needs course-specific edits, do not edit it in place;
copy the section you need into `my-content/chapters/` (see
`tools/extract_section.py`) and edit the copy. Otherwise the next regeneration
will silently discard your edits.

## Building and previewing

```bash
cd yr-materials
quarto preview            # live-reloading local server
quarto render             # writes the site to yr-materials/_book/
```

`tools/build.sh` regenerates the chapters, runs a few sanity checks (balanced
code fences, exactly one level-one heading per chapter), and renders.
Build output is ignored by Git.

## Pulling updates from upstream

```bash
git fetch upstream
git merge upstream/master
python3 yr-materials/tools/mkd2qmd.py
git push origin master
```

`tools/sync_upstream.sh` does all of this and prints which chapters changed.

## Adding a chapter of our own

```bash
python3 yr-materials/tools/new_chapter.py invoices "Working with invoice data"
```

This creates `my-content/chapters/invoices.qmd` with the standard header and
inserts it into `_quarto.yml` between the `my-content chapters` markers. Move
the line within `_quarto.yml` to place the chapter where you want it in the
reading order.

To lift a section from a py4e chapter as a starting point:

```bash
python3 yr-materials/tools/extract_section.py 05 "The while statement" \
        --out my-content/chapters/while-loops.qmd
```

## Course design notes

The course follows Allen Downey's *Think Python* (3rd edition) for its early
chapters and uses this book as a supplement. Guidelines for new material:

- Students are business majors. Prefer examples about sales, invoices,
  customers, budgets, and spreadsheets over geometry or number theory.
- Loops are taught before conditionals, following *Think Python*. Chapter 5
  (Iteration) of this book fits that stage well: it covers `while`, `for`,
  and the counting, summing, and max/min patterns without any mathematics
  beyond arithmetic.
- Avoid turtle-graphics exercises that require angle calculations.
